channel.description: Latest articles from Literary Review of Canada (reviewcanada.ca)

item.title: Desperately Seeking Space Friends | A review of “The Pale Blue Data Point” by Jon Willis | Literary Review of Canada
item.description: Dan Falk reviews “The Pale Blue Data Point” by Jon Willis, a book on the existence of extraterrestrial life and our search for cosmic truth.

item.title: They Were Not What They Were | A review of “Canada and the Blackface Atlantic” by Cheryl Thompson | Literary Review of Canada
item.description: Andrew Torry reviews “Canada and the Blackface Atlantic” by Cheryl Thompson, a book on minstrelsy in Canadian theatre from 1812 to 1897.

item.title: Dear Mabs | A review of “Till We Meet Again” by Brandon Marriott | Literary Review of Canada
item.description: Ruth Panofsky reviews “Till We Meet Again” by Brandon Marriott, a book on one soldier’s Great War correspondence.

item.title: Behind the Wire | A review of “No Place like Home” by Bohdan S. Kordan | Literary Review of Canada
item.description: J. L. Granatstein reviews “No Place like Home” by Bohdan S. Kordan, a book on Ukrainian internment in Canada during the First World War.

item.title: House of Card | A review of “Thirsty Land into Springs of Water” by Brooke Kathleen Brassard | Literary Review of Canada
item.description: Michael Ledger-Lomas reviews “Thirsty Land into Springs of Water” by Brooke Kathleen Brassard, a book on Mormon settlement in Canada.

item.title: They Desire a Better System A review of “A New Blueprint for Government” by Kevin G. Lynch and James R. Mitchell and “Statecraft” by Stephen Azzi and Patrice Dutil | Literary Review of Canada
item.description: Aaron Wherry reviews two books on reshaping the prime minister’s office. He insists political leaders are the ones who must engender these changes in Parliament.
